artifacts.summary: Research on gate-8 timing ceiling, gate-lock fail-open posture, load-adaptive gate bounds, advisory-vs-mechanical batch gate deferral, and the orchestrator's unbounded wait on its own dispatched agents.

memory_candidates.content: verify-deploy.sh's gate8_run() already implements a load-aware contention-tagging mechanism (GATE8_CONTENTION_DETECTED), triggered by either the .gate-lock acquire wait time (>= 10% of GATE_MUTEX_ACQUIRE_BUDGET_MS, i.e. >=60s of the 600s default) or the entry 1-minute loadavg (>= 2.0, GATE8_CONTENTION_LOAD_THRESHOLD, matching measure-gate-costs.sh's own MEASURE_GATE_COSTS_LOAD_THRESHOLD default). It only annotates Gate 8's own finding as WARN-FINDING [CONTENTION] rather than adjusting the timeout bound, and no other gate in gate-registry.data has an equivalent -- this is the precedent shape to extend rather than inventing a new load-adaptive mechanism for the other 29 gates' fixed 30-180s timeouts.

measure-gate-costs.sh is the existing, checked-in, load-gated (default threshold 2.0 on the 1-minute loadavg), per-run-contamination-detecting, overwrite-protected averaging harness for per-gate/per-suite wall-clock baselines (writes scripts/gate-cost-model.csv and, via --regen-hints, scripts/tests/suite-cost-hints.txt). Any future need to re-measure a gate or the full battery's wall-clock should reuse this script rather than building a new ad hoc timing harness; it already refuses (exit 2) to record a measurement taken above the load threshold.

skill-orchestrate's Move 2 issues every dispatch[]/aux_dispatch[] row's Agent call in ONE message, and Move 3 (postflight, which is also where stall_suspected is computed from orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's JSON) runs only 'after ALL Agent calls from Move 2 complete' per SKILL.md's own text. This means stall detection is structurally wired downstream of the exact event (a dispatch returning) it needs to detect the absence of -- a silent sibling dispatch blocks postflight for every task in the wave, not just its own, and no per-dispatch timeout exists anywhere in this path today. Fixing it requires confirming whether the orchestrator's own top-level session (not a dispatched subagent, whose own Agent tool explicitly lacks run_in_background) has a background/async Agent-dispatch capability it could poll instead.
